extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: WikiText is a benchmark dataset for language modeling extracted from text on Wikipedia. It consists of articles meeting Wikipedia's Good or Featured criteria, preserves punctuation, casing, and numbers, and is split into two sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103 to evaluate language models on long-term dependencies and realistic vocabularies.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia were selected, resulting in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Good and Featured articles extracted from Wikipedia markup via the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Specific sections primarily featuring lists were removed by default. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to split numbers (e.g., 8,600 to 8 @,@ 600) with minor fixes. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding words with a count below 3, mapping words outside of the vocabulary to the <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of language models, specifically for evaluating how well models exploit longer contexts, deal with realistic vocabularies, rare words, and long-term dependencies.
